candidates.title: ‘Speed kills’ vs. ‘just do it:’ Survey illustrates Albertans’ hopes, fears over highway speed
candidates.description: Two thirds of Albertans who filled out a survey on highway speed limits last year said they supported increasing the speed limit on rural divided highways to 120 km/h, but the results show older drivers were less likely than younger ones to support the idea.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: What Trump's 'most favoured nation' drug pricing policy might mean for Canadians
candidates.description: To avoid triggering massive U.S. price cuts, pharmaceutical companies now incentivized to protect their larger U.S. profits by raising prices elsewhere, drug policy experts say.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Tragically Hip, Feist and more inducted into Canadian Songwriters Hall of Fame
candidates.description: The memory of the late Gord Downie was in sharp focus as the Kingston alt-rock band the Tragically Hip were among four musical acts inducted into the Canadian Songwriters Hall of Fame at a star-studded gala held at Toronto's Massey Hall on Saturday night.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Behold the pawpaw, the tropical ‘alien banana’ that grows right here in Canada
candidates.description: The pawpaw fruit tastes of banana, mango and pineapple and was once abundant across parts of North America, but it can still be found growing wild and in some orchards.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Mycelium with your meatballs? How one Vancouver company is farming fungi to combat the cost of cow
candidates.description: A Vancouver-based company has figured out a way to grow and harvest mycelium — the hidden, underground root-like networks of fungus that give rise to mushrooms. The result is a food product that can add bulk to meat products.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Could a single Maritime power grid make electricity more reliable?
candidates.description: When Canada's premiers met in Prince Edward Island back in July, leaders from the Maritime provinces had power on their minds — just not the political kind.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Poilievre urges tax cuts to make diesel fuel more affordable
candidates.description: Conservative Leader Pierre Poilievre is pitching a plan to cut federal taxes on diesel fuel and help ensure Canada has affordable supplies of the fuel in the future.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Canada's Leylah Fernandez wins Singapore Open for 1st title of season
candidates.description: Canada's Leylah Fernandez captured her first title of the season with a 7-5, 6-0 win over Australia's Talia Gibson in the women's singles final at the Singapore Tennis Open on Sunday.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Albertans divided on immigration, while half still undecided on 9 non-separation questions: poll
candidates.description: Albertans are divided over immigration but attitudes are “softening,” while nearly half still don’t know which way they’ll vote on the nine non-separation questions in the Oct. 19 referendum, a new poll commissioned by CBC News suggests.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Whistleblower alleges millions of Driscoll’s berries sent to Canada with excess chemical levels
candidates.description: A whistleblower lawsuit in California is alleging millions of pounds of Driscoll's fruit containing non-compliant levels of pesticides and chemicals crossed the border into Canada, and the company tried to cover it up.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Helicopter crashes outside Montreal, killing all 4 occupants
candidates.description: Police are investigating after a helicopter crashed in a field near the Rang des Écossais in the municipality of Sainte-Brigide-d’Iberville on Saturday afternoon.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: What Canada's wastewater reveals about drug use in 8 cities
candidates.description: New StatCan data shows sharply different drug-use patterns across eight Canadian cities, with methamphetamine elevated in parts of the Prairies and Moncton, cocaine comparatively high in Halifax and fentanyl highest in Metro Vancouver.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: First Nation chiefs in northern Ontario rally around Neskantaga amid ongoing evacuation
candidates.description: It’s been nearly eight weeks since Neskantaga First Nation’s most vulnerable members were sent to a hotel in Toronto, but remediation work on the nursing station that forced the evacuation has only just begun. That's left some community members worrying they won't get home before the snow falls. The remote Ojibway community, some 440 kilometres northeast of Thunder Bay, Ont., declared a state of emergency on Aug. 4 following a sewage spill at its nursing station, the only health-care facility in the First Nation. Here's the latest on the situation.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: B.C. man uses motion-activated zombie to scare bears away from garbage
candidates.description: More than 33 bears have been killed by conservation officers in B.C. this year, including two that entered stores through automatic sliding doors in Hope and Squamish. It's led to creative solutions to keep the hungry animals away from attractants.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Eyesore from oil and gas era being dismantled in Tuktoyaktuk, N.W.T.
candidates.description: A forty-foot steel structure used for oil and gas exploration in the Beaufort Delta has been moved for the first time in decades.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Montreal squirrels change their coat colour depending on neighbourhood they live in, new study finds
candidates.description: A new McGill study found that eastern grey squirrels in the city vary in coat colour depending on the neighbourhood they live in. The animals are influenced by local environmental conditions, including temperature and forest cover.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: B.C. family still looking for answers 1 month after deadly Nepal flood
candidates.description: Over 1,400 bodies have been recovered and over 5,600 people remain missing — the Canadian Press reports — a month after a catastrophic flash flood struck the Himalayan border between Nepal and Tibet on Aug. 26.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: How do you grow N.L.'s population? Province wants feedback as fertility rate hits record low
candidates.description: The provincial government wants more people in Newfoundland and Labrador, as fertility rates hit an all-time low and population growth slows amid federal cuts to immigration.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Ottawa Titans crowned Frontier League champions for 1st time
candidates.description: For the first time in franchise history, the Ottawa Titans are the Frontier League champions, shutting out the Evansville Otters in Game 4 of the finals in front of thousands of passionate fans.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Supporters from both sides of border demand better Canada-U.S. relations as B.C. election heats up
candidates.description: Canadians, Americans and dual citizens gathered at the Peace Arch border Saturday, calling for better relations between the two countries as Canada-U.S. trade tensions remain a key issue in B.C.’s election campaign. The group has met every two weeks at Peace Arch Park since March 2025.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: U.K. police arrest 5 near airbase used by U.S. on suspicion of preparing a terrorist act
candidates.description: British police arrested five men near an airbase used by the U.S. on suspicion of explosive and terrorism offenses on Sunday after a tip-off that three vans had been heading to the military airfield, which has been used to strike Iran.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Bill Gates joins call for AI safeguards, wants to discuss concerns with Trump
candidates.description: AI requires safeguards that go beyond self-regulation, ‌Microsoft co-founder Bill Gates said in an interview that aired on Sunday, calling for legislation to be passed in Congress. A groundswell has ​risen in favour of federal intervention after OpenAI said in July an autonomous AI agent went rogue during a security test and hacked into another company
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Vucic resigns as Serbia president, setting up election that could see him become PM
candidates.description: Serbia's populist President Aleksandar Vucic resigned on Sunday to pursue a bid to become the prime minister in an upcoming early parliamentary election that will test his firm rule in the Balkan country after nearly two years of protests.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Putin appears to be eyeing NATO. The question is, will he actually attack?
candidates.description: European military experts warn that Russia is actively planning targeted aggression against NATO to test alliance solidarity. Recent high-alert incidents include a foiled explosive drone plot at a German airport and a strike near the Ukraine-Poland border targeting European VIPs. However, officials are deeply split on the immediacy of a conventional threat.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Tensions run high in Northern Ireland after contentious march given go-ahead
candidates.description: British Prime Minister Andy Burnham called for calm in Northern Ireland on Sunday after a contentious parade was given the go-ahead by the High Court in Belfast in a late-night sitting.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: South African police probe mining feud, business rivalry after shootings kill 27
candidates.description: South African police on Sunday were hunting the perpetrators of two separate shootings that killed 27 people within hours of each other, highlighting the country's gun violence problem.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: OpenAI pauses training of latest models after AI agents probed U.S. government sites in unexpected ways
candidates.description: OpenAI said it has paused training of its latest artificial intelligence models as reports of AI agents going rogue mount.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Swiss voters reject tighter neutrality rules that would have curbed NATO co-operation
candidates.description: Swiss voters on Sunday looked set to reject a proposal to adopt a more restrictive form of neutrality that would have blocked their ​country from imposing economic sanctions or co-operating with NATO.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Why is it so difficult for Ukraine to take down Russia's jet-powered drones?
candidates.description: Russia's jet-powered drones being used to carry out strikes on Kyiv and other parts of Ukraine are often able to evade air defences because they fly at higher altitudes and faster speeds. To stop these new models, faster interceptors are needed, but that technology is still in the trial phase, Ukrainian officials say.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Palestinian death toll in Gaza war rises above 74,000 since war began
candidates.description: While a ceasefire that took effect last Oct. 10 has halted the heaviest fighting, Israeli strikes have continued in what the military has said are responses to threats or attacks.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Trump rejects Iranian proposal to open Strait of Hormuz and end fighting
candidates.description: U.S. President Donald Trump said on Saturday he had rejected an Iranian proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and end fighting in the Middle East.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: China, U.S. agree to AI dialogue, tariff cuts on $30 billion in goods during Xi visit
candidates.description: The United States and China have agreed to reduce tariffs on $30 billion US of goods and launch a dialogue on AI, both countries said following President Xi Jinping's visit to Washington.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Powerful storm causes widespread flooding, outages in northeast U.S.
candidates.description: A slow-moving, powerful storm crept along the coast of the northeast U.S. on Saturday, producing high winds that knocked out electricity to tens of thousands while whipping up big waves and heavy rains that created dangerous conditions in some places.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: In UN address, Anand takes jab at 'great powers' disrupting global order
candidates.description: Foreign Affairs Minister Anita Anand has put "strategic autonomy" at the forefront of Canada's address to the United Nations General Assembly today.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: China pushes back against U.S. on Iran, Cuba in UN speech
candidates.description: China pushed back against the United States in its speech at the UN General Assembly on Saturday, saying sovereignty of countries in the Gulf should be respected and urging the "relevant country" to stop threatening Cuba and lift its blockade on it.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Mothers crossing the Mexico-U.S. border risk everything to reunite with their children
candidates.description: While the migrant caravans may have disappeared from Tijuana, and this Mexican border city is no longer the waiting room for entry into the U.S., there are still those seeking to cross. Many who risk the journey are deported mothers desperate to get back to their children, advocates say.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: What is the truth about Diana? Her brother offers his view, ‘once and for all’
candidates.description: The recent publication of a book by Charles Spencer, the younger brother of the late Diana, Princess of Wales, has only added to the way in which her legacy will keep being a focus of debate and interpretation as time keeps passing on from her sudden death in 1997.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Hundreds of thousands turn out for Pope Leo along Champs-Élysées ahead of mass in Paris
candidates.description: Hundreds of thousands of people packed Paris's iconic Champs-Élysées avenue for Pope Leo XIV's big outdoor mass on Saturday, a sign of the Catholic Church's enduring appeal in the once staunchly Catholic but officially secular country.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: The incoming U.S. import bans on Canadian alcohol, whey, molasses and motorcycles, by the numbers
candidates.description: The United States is set to ban a select number of Canadian imports starting Tuesday, in the next escalation of a trade war that has already led to steep tariffs on goods from both sides.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Iranian minister says only negotiation can end conflict after Trump rejects Hormuz deal
candidates.description: The foreign minister says Tehran is waiting for an official rejection of a deal, despite the US President's comments.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Two mass shootings in South Africa leave 27 dead
candidates.description: The two attacks hours apart come as the country struggles to stop high levels of gang-related armed violence.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Killer Christa Pike to be executed within days - but her defence say she's a victim too
candidates.description: Lawyers for Pike, who killed a fellow student in 1995, say she should get clemency and would not be sentenced to death if the crime happened today.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Two bodies found after avalanche hits Himalayan climbing group
candidates.description: Rescuers are looking for at least 10 Nepalese people who were preparing to take climbers up the Himlung Himal peak.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: One dead as nor'easter storm pummels New York and New Jersey
candidates.description: Tens of millions of people from Maine to Virginia found themselves in the path of the powerful weather system.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Venezuela releases dozens of political prisoners as election calls grow
candidates.description: A slew of dissidents being released from long-term detention comes days after the nation's interim leader met the US president.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Woman charged with stealing from patients and staff at hospitals across Ontario
candidates.description: The 34-year-old is under investigation for incidents that began in February 2024 up until as recently as last month.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Mother of woman found hanging in tree shocked as police say body was staged
candidates.description: Christy Spivey tells the BBC she only has more questions now police think Tasia Fortune's body was put in the tree after her death.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Brazil's Lula bans online gambling ahead of presidential election
candidates.description: Lula, who is currently in a tight presidential race against Flávio Bolsonaro, said the industry was a "cancer" that he must "remove".
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Before BTS and Blackpink, there was Big Bang: Now the Kings of K-pop are back
candidates.description: Big Bang played London's Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, marking a long-awaited return for the group that helped build the blueprint for modern K-pop.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: What is kratom, the 'gas station heroin' alarming officials in the US?
candidates.description: Kratom, found during an investigation into the deaths of two college students, has been sold in the US for around a decade.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Are claims of a white genocide in South Africa real?
candidates.description: Thousands of white crosses have been displayed in Washington by an Afrikaner lobby group But South Africa's new ambassador Roelf Meyer says there is not a genocide.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Watch: Bangkok declared flood disaster zone
candidates.description: Heavy rain over the last two days has overwhelmed Bangkok's water systems, with more rain forecast on Sunday.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Inside iconic horror game Silent Hill's Scottish makeover
candidates.description: One of gaming's biggest horror franchises has come to the UK. Can it live up to the original?
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Your pictures of the Harvest Moon shimmering across the UK sky
candidates.description: The full Moon put on a stunning display over the skies of UK on Saturday night and here are some of your photographs.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Amid changing dynamics in the Middle East, Turkey seeks to emerge as a leader
candidates.description: Turkey's attempts at expanding its Middle East footprint has put it in a position of power, coming head-to-head with Israel.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Playing 'La Bamba' for an hour? Must be a Mexican fandango!
candidates.description: A 300-year-old Mexican musical tradition is finding new life around the world — one sweaty, joyous, all-night fandango at a time.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Photos: This may be the most inspirational night school on Earth
candidates.description: Many thousands of boys and men in Lesotho take up the vital profession of herding but have to give up their education. A small network of schools on a shoestring budget is teaching them the ABCs.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: 5 arrested near a U.K. air base used by U.S. on suspicion of preparing a terrorist act
candidates.description: Police evacuated homes Sunday near an air base in England used by the U.S. and arrested several men over suspected explosives offenses.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Trump gave Xi Jinping a warm welcome. What did the talks accomplish?
candidates.description: From the National Archives to the state dinner, President Trump and Xi Jinping looked comfortable together in Washington. Two former NPR China correspondents on what the visit did and didn't deliver.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Is Congo's Ebola outbreak coming under control?
candidates.description: Four months in, Congo's Ebola outbreak is one of the largest ever recorded. Officials and outside experts can't agree on whether it's finally slowing down.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Trump calls Iranian plan to reopen Strait of Hormuz not 'acceptable'
candidates.description: President Trump said he was rejecting an Iranian plan to reopen the Strait of Hormuz. The Iranian proposal is similar to a memorandum of understanding agreed upon by the U.S. and Iran back in June.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Why this island paradise has the world's fastest-growing HIV epidemic
candidates.description: In mid-September, Fiji's government declared a national emergency because of a startling rise in HIV infections. The country's crystal meth epidemic is a strong contributing factor.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Pope warns a 'paradise of machines' could undermine humanity as he opens France trip
candidates.description: Pope Leo XIV has warned that a "paradise of machines" could undermine humanity. He raises concerns about artificial intelligence, nuclear arms, and human rights during his visit to France.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Everyone is racing to create an AI device. Meta thinks it has one
candidates.description: Tech companies are betting that people will connect with AI using something other than smartphones. Meta is going all-in on glasses, after launching its new AI agent Muse.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Aga's restaurant in Houston is number one in the world for Uber Eats deliveries
candidates.description: In Houston, Aga's Indian-Pakistani restaurant serves around 4,000 meals a day and according to Uber Eats, it has the most takeout orders in the world on the their platform.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: From professor to patient: One man's journey on the frontier of lung cancer treatment
candidates.description: Lung cancer is still the top cancer killer, but new developments are shifting what the future might hold for patients.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Meal deliveries can save money and improve health. Will they survive Medicaid cuts?
candidates.description: Some states deliver meals to Medicaid patients that address their dietary needs. Evidence shows it aids recovery and saves healthcare costs, but federal budget cuts may lead some states to cancel it.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: The U.S. has more thalidomide survivors than the government admits
candidates.description: In the 1950s and 1960s, doctors gave the drug thalidomide to pregnant patients without telling them — and without FDA approval. Now those patients' children want recognition.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.description: The United States Geological Survey reported an earthquake of magnitude 6.6. The event occurred near 80 km ENE of Tadine, New Caledonia. Official monitoring data may be updated as scientists review additional measurements.
